questions.q: Which five powers make up Moore's hierarchy, in order of importance?
a: Category, company, market, offer, execution
Product, price, place, promotion, people
Vision, culture, hiring, process, cash
Market, category, execution, offer, company
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the five powers from category down to execution.

questions.q: Why did Newsweek sell for a dollar while 3Par sold for billions?
a: Storage was a growing category and print media was not
Newsweek carried far more debt than 3Par
3Par owned patents that Newsweek lacked
Newsweek had lost its readers to television
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses both sales to show category power at work.

questions.q: What single question determines a company's category power?
a: Is your industry growing or shrinking?
Is your team the best in the field?
Can customers easily substitute your product?
Are your margins better than rivals'?
questions.why: Lesson 2 reduces category power to whether the industry is growing.

questions.q: Besides differentiation, what two activities build offer power?
a: Neutralization and optimization
Advertising and discounting
Hiring and training
Outsourcing and automation
questions.why: Lesson 3 names differentiation, neutralization and optimization.

questions.q: Which examples does Moore give of a 10x improvement?
a: Free Skype calls and Wikipedia's wider access
Apple cutting headset prices to match rivals
Domino's opening more stores than competitors
Newsweek moving its magazine online
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites Skype's free calls and Wikipedia's accessibility as 10x gains.
